replication.target_description: The description identifies the crowd within phenomenon and p. 6, but does not identify a condition, single-guess comparator, or between-condition contrast. Table 4 has four crowd-within tests; nearby text adds further comparisons. Target correspondence is unresolved; selecting by order or numbers would be unjustified.

n.exclusions: Immediate: 484 recruited, 11 incomplete and 2 looking up answers excluded; final 471. Delayed: 231 first session, 171 also second; 9 incomplete, 21 defocusing browser and 1 looking up answers excluded; final 140. Impossible/blank answers prevented rather than excluded.
n.quote: Our final sample of 471 psychology students consisted ... Our final sample of 140 ... participants consisted of 125 women and 15 men

reported_success.quote: the current study can be considered as a successful ... replication of the crowd within effect, in both the immediate and ... the delayed condition.

notes: Identity verified independently from supplied primary text: title Measuring the crowd within again: a pre-registered replication study; Sara Steegen, Laura Dewitte, Francis Tuerlinckx and Wolf Vanpaemel; published 28 July 2014, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00786. Primary report includes methods, results, tables, discussion and references; appended corrigendum (2015, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2015.00238) corrects planned sample sizes only, not final samples. No local PDF supplied; no rendering or acquisition. Original side unassigned placeholder, not an availability determination. All printed candidate test statistics are t statistics; no metric conversion. Candidates with same-test p bounds: [{"test": "Immediate guess 1 versus average", "n": "471", "t": "8.69", "df": "470", "p": "0.001", "bound": "l"}, {"test": "Immediate guess 2 versus average", "n": "471", "t": "10.26", "df": "470", "p": "0.001", "bound": "l"}, {"test": "Delayed guess 1 versus average", "n": "140", "t": "4.02", "df": "139", "p": "0.001", "bound": "l"}, {"test": "Delayed guess 2 versus average", "n": "140", "t": "8.48", "df": "139", "p": "0.001", "bound": "l"}, {"test": "Immediate guess 1 versus guess 2", "n": "471", "t": "−2.25", "df": "470", "p": "0.025", "bound": "e"}, {"test": "Delayed guess 1 versus guess 2", "n": "140", "t": "−2.91", "df": "139", "p": "0.004", "bound": "e"}, {"test": "Between conditions: accuracy gain relative to guess 1", "candidate_n": "611", "t": "0.18", "df": "609", "p": "0.858", "bound": "e"}, {"test": "Between conditions: accuracy gain relative to guess 2, post-hoc", "candidate_n": "611", "t": "3.14", "df": "609", "p": "0.002", "bound": "e"}]. Candidate between-condition N only: 471 immediate participants + 140 delayed participants = 611 participants. These are explicitly separate final condition groups (p. 5; Table 5 p. 7 labels 471 (n1) & 140 (n2)). No analytic N assigned because the locator does not establish a between-condition test. Within-condition candidate analytic Ns are 471 and 140. No N derived from df. Immediate: 484 recruited, 11 incomplete and 2 looking up answers excluded; final 471. Delayed: 231 first session, 171 also second; 9 incomplete, 21 defocusing browser and 1 looking up answers excluded; final 140. Impossible/blank answers prevented rather than excluded. Authors call the crowd within replication successful in both conditions; the separate temporal-delay magnitude question has mixed evidence (p. 7).
